title: Insurance Claim Services: The Insured's Dwelling Depreciation Release from the Claim Portal
content:
**Scope.** This Insurance Claim Services policy prices the insured's dwelling release: the depreciation release request on the dwelling coverage that the insured submits from the company's claim portal on a Public Adjuster Coordinated Claim Billing file, where the company does not request depreciation itself, naming the file's reconstruction contract as the completed job, for an insured who holds exactly one water mitigation job and exactly one reconstruction contract, both linked to the file, on which no price variance or scope omission supplement has yet been decided and every supplement of any other reason has been decided. Any other release request is handled under the base release rule.

## Conditions of the request

- The claim file must be in approved status when a depreciation release is requested.
- The job named in the request must be complete: a rebuild contract in substantially complete, final invoiced or closed status.
- A depreciation release may be requested only no later than the depreciation window after the first ACV payment was received on the claim file, counted in calendar days starting the day after the received date of the earliest ACV carrier payment on the file, a request submitted on the last day of the window being in time.

## The amount requested

For an insured's dwelling release this policy prices, and only for such a release, the amount requested is the release figure; every other release request, a contents release and every release the company submits included, requests the depreciation withheld on the approvals of that coverage part less any depreciation already released on it.

## When the release figure is worked out

The insured's depreciation release is not computed before the credited-line write-off owed on the initial dwelling approval has been worked out and, where it comes to more than nothing and within the desk write-off cap, posted.

The insured's depreciation release is fixed only after the category reassessment supplement owed for the water job has been prepared and, where it reaches the supplement minimum, recorded on the file.

The insured's depreciation release waits until the regulated-scope supplement owed for the water job has been prepared and, where it reaches the supplement minimum, recorded on the file.

## The insured's request: `submit_depreciation_release_d117c1f9`

**Capability.** The insured submits to their insurance carrier, from the company's claim portal, a request to release the recoverable depreciation the carrier withheld on the dwelling coverage of their claim file, naming the completed reconstruction contract as proof of completion. One call records one depreciation release request on the dwelling coverage, dated today, carrying the amount requested; it then shows on the claim file as submitted. Nothing on the contract or on the carrier receivable changes.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks `submit_depreciation_release_d117c1f9` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it from the claim portal.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `claim_file_id` | the reference number of the insured's claim file, as returned by the claim file lookup for this customer | identifier |
| `related_job_id` | the reference number of the completed reconstruction contract the request names, as returned by the reconstruction contract lookup for this claim file | identifier |
| `requested_amount` | the depreciation the request asks the carrier to release, in US dollars | a positive number with 2 decimal places; more places are rounded half up to the cent when recorded |

**Return.** A confirmation naming the request reference, the claim file reference, the completed contract reference, the coverage dwelling, the submission date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the amount requested (US dollars, two decimals); it means the release request is on the claim file. A reply starting with "Error:" means nothing was recorded (a `requested_amount` that is not a positive number of US dollars, or an unknown claim file).
